questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving async — timers.

stimulus.body: A program is processing the value 2893.

options.misconception: Treating a zero delay as immediate

questions.explanation: setTimeout schedules its callback as a macrotask, so both synchronous logs finish before 2893 appears. A delay of zero does not mean run right now. The printed value is 1 3 2893, while the alternatives come from treating a zero delay as immediate, reversing the synchronous statements and placing the timer callback first.
questions.hint: Timers run after the current synchronous stack clears.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving errors — try catch finally.

answer.exemplar: The throw enters catch, which logs 'caught', and finally always runs afterwards with 'done'. The finally block executes whether or not an error was thrown. The result is caught done.

questions.explanation: The throw enters catch, which logs 'caught', and finally always runs afterwards with 'done'. The finally block executes whether or not an error was thrown. A complete answer names caught done and justifies it from the code rather than guessing.
questions.hint: finally runs after catch, even on the error path.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — numeric sort.

options.misconception: Assuming sort leaves the original order

questions.explanation: The comparator subtracts to sort numerically ascending, placing the smallest value 2 first. Without a comparator, sort would compare the numbers as strings. The printed value is 2, while the alternatives come from assuming sort leaves the original order, picking the middle value and applies a different mistaken operation.
questions.hint: A comparator returning a minus b sorts numbers ascending.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — index of.

options.misconception: Assuming the value is not found

questions.explanation: indexOf returns the zero-based position of the first match; 2897 sits at index zero here. A missing value would yield negative one instead. The printed value is 0, while the alternatives come from using one-based indexing, assuming the value is not found and reporting the array length.
questions.hint: JavaScript array positions begin at zero.
